signals.title: AUD/USD — G10 Scorecard + TIER-1 News + Vol
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7016, holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster following a massive TIER-1 beat in Australian household spending (+0.8% vs +0.2% expected) and strong Job Ads data. This domestic outperformance surfaces as the G10 scorecard shows a -60bp carry disadvantage for AUD vs USD, yet AUD/USD remains resilient. Options markets are pricing significant tail-risk with a +9.1% Vol Risk Premium (IV 15.7% vs HV30 6.6%), signaling that protection against an AUD breakout is becoming expensive. COT LF net long +23,616 (64.1% long) aligns with the hawkish RBA bias, while retail remains 64% short, providing a contrarian tailwind for further upside. RBA holds at 4.35%. Risk: A reversal in global risk-on sentiment (VIX > 20) forces a carry-led liquidation of AUD longs.

signals.title: CAD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Geopolitical Risk
signals.text: CAD/JPY trades at 112.202 as the G10 bilateral theme reaches a critical spread of 2.534%, driven by JPY outperformance (+1.797%) and CAD weakness (-0.737%). While a +125bp OIS carry premium favors CAD, geopolitical tensions in the Strait of Hormuz—with Iran rejecting second corridors and threatening military force—are driving haven demand for JPY. JPY's performance is further supported by a strong ESI (+22.9), contrasting with the market's heavy COT LF net short of -124,575. This positioning leaves the pair highly vulnerable to a disorderly short-squeeze if geopolitical threats escalate. USD/JPY remains comfortably below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 157.59, confirming the broad yen strength. Risk: De-escalation in the Middle East restores focus to the 125bp carry advantage, stalling the JPY bid.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + Carry + Retail Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY at 157.59 continues to trade with a heavy downside bias in the options market, where the 25d RR at -3.19 shows a strong put skew despite a massive +275bp Fed-BoJ carry advantage. The volatility regime remains unusual with a negative VRP of -1.1% (IV 7.2% vs HV30 8.3%), suggesting the options market is complacent regarding the scale of recent realized moves. Speculative positioning (COT) remains significantly net short JPY (-124,575), but retail traders are currently 72% long USD/JPY, creating a sharp institutional-vs-retail divergence. With price currently below the SMA20 (162.34) and SMA50 (161.31), the technical trend is firmly bearish. Risk: A break back above the 160.00 psychological level invalidates the bearish momentum and triggers retail capitulation.

signals.title: NZD/USD — COT-OIS Divergence + ESI
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5869, currently positioned above its SMA20/50/200 cluster following a period of sustained data beats reflected in its ESI of +33.4. RBNZ holds at 2.5%. This crowded speculative short is at risk of a squeeze if upcoming data confirms the need for further RBNZ tightening, especially as the real policy rate remains accommodative at -1.56%. Retail sentiment is also 66% short, aligning with the contrarian bullish signal from the institutional short-squeeze setup. Watch the 0.5826 level (SMA200) as key support. Risk: RBNZ shifts to a neutral bias, validating the speculative short positioning.

signals.title: USD/CHF — Volatility Risk Premium Extreme
signals.text: USD/CHF trades at 0.8098, characterized by an extreme Vol Risk Premium of +18.8% (IV 25.1% vs HV30 6.3%). This massive gap indicates the options market is paying a significant premium for tail-risk protection compared to actual realized price action. While the +375bp Fed-SNB carry differential remains the widest in the G10 space, the Swiss Franc is seeing renewed interest due to Middle East headlines and its safe-haven status. Technically, the pair is holding below its SMA20 (0.8106) but above its SMA50/200. COT positioning shows a modest net short in CHF of -11,635, which does not yet reflect an extreme. Risk: A return to 'normal volatility' leads to a rapid collapse in IV, favoring a carry-led USD/CHF recovery.
